q: 1. The canals meant for the purpose of draining off water from water logged areas are called .............
explain: Drains (or drainage canals) are specifically designed to lower the water table and remove excess surface or sub-surface water to prevent waterlogging.

q: 2. For effective control of silt entry into the canal the sill of the head regulator should be .............
options: below the sill of the under sluices
above the sill of the under sluices
at the same level as the sill of the under sluices
explain: By keeping the head regulator sill higher than the under-sluice sill, the heavier silt-laden water stays at the bottom and passes through the sluices, while cleaner surface water enters the canal.

q: 3. According to Kennedy's theory the critical velocity is proportional to (if D is the depth of flow) .............
explain: Kennedy's equation for critical velocity is V0 = 0.55 * m * D^0.64, where m is the critical velocity ratio and D is the depth of water.

q: 4. If Q is the discharge and f is the silt factor, the regime scour depth according to Lacey's theory is given by .............
explain: Lacey's regime scour depth formula for a wide channel is R = 1.35 * (q^2/f)^(1/3), where q is discharge per unit width.

q: 5. If w is the unit weight of water, S is the bed slope and R is the hydraulic radius, the average tractive force on the canal bed is given by .............
explain: Tractive force (or shear stress) is calculated as Tau = Gamma * R * S, which represents the force exerted by flowing water on the wetted surface.

q: 6. The purpose of the cross-regulator is .............
options: to control the discharge into the off-take canal
to maintain proper levels in the main canal
to control the silt entry into the off-take canal
explain: A cross-regulator is built across the main canal (downstream of an off-take) to head up water and maintain sufficient depth to feed the off-taking canal during low flow.

q: 7. When canal runs above the drain, the cross drainage work provided is .............
explain: An aqueduct is a bridge-like structure where the canal water is carried over a natural drainage stream.

q: 8. When the canal runs below the drain, the cross drainage work provided is called .............
explain: A super passage is the reverse of an aqueduct; here, the natural drain water is carried in a trough over the canal.

q: 9. In the case of an aqueduct if the canal section (including banks) is not changed, then it is called .............
explain: In Type I aqueducts, the canal section remains unaltered as it crosses the drain, usually requiring a very long structure.

q: 10. In the type III aqueduct, the splay of the d/s transition canal is .............
explain: The downstream transition (expansion) is made more gradual than the upstream one to minimize head loss and turbulence, typically using a splay of 3:1.

q: 11. According to Lacey's theory the regime velocity is proportional to .............
explain: The regime velocity in Lacey's theory is expressed as V = (R^(2/3) * S^(1/2)) / n, which is similar to the Manning's formula for flow.

q: 12. The ratio of rate of change of discharge in the outlet to the rate of change of the water level in the distributory with respect to the normal depth of flow is called .............
explain: Sensitivity measures how an outlet's discharge responds to changes in the supply canal's water level.

q: 13. The full supply level (F.S.L.) of a gravity canal is .............
options: about 4 to 5 m above the ground level
explain: For gravity irrigation to be effective, the water level in the canal must be slightly higher than the fields it intends to irrigate.

q: 14. The berms formed finally in the canals will serve the purpose of .............
explain: Berms provide a horizontal transition that acts as a cushion for waves, reduces the pressure on the outer banks, and helps the phreatic line stay within the bank section.

q: 15. Disposal of excess excavated earth is used to make spoil bank on .............
explain: Spoil banks are constructed on both or either side of the canal when the volume of cutting significantly exceeds the volume of bank filling required.

q: 16. A weir in which the tail water level is less than the crest level is called
explain: In a free-flow (or free) weir, the tail water level is below the crest, allowing the nappe to discharge freely into the air.

q: 17. A fall in which the crest is kept at or near the canal bed without any glacis, is
explain: A trapezoidal notch fall consists of a wall across the canal with one or more notches; it is designed to maintain the depth-discharge relationship without a sloping glacis.

q: 18. The degree of sinuosity is the ratio between the
options: meander length and width of meander
meander length and width of river
curved length and straight air distance
explain: Sinuosity is a measure of how much a river meanders; it is calculated as the ratio of the actual channel length (curved) to the shortest axial distance (straight line).

q: 19. In Lanes weighted creep theory the weights proposed for horizontal and vertical creeps are in the ratio of
explain: Lane suggested that horizontal creep is less effective in reducing uplift than vertical creep. He gave a weight of 1/3 to horizontal creep and 1 to vertical creep (3H:1V).

q: 20. Outlet discharge for a particular crop is given by
explain: Discharge = Area / Duty. In this context, 'Outlet factor' is another term for duty at the outlet.

q: 21. The fall of moisture from the atmosphere to the earth surface in any form, is called
explain: Precipitation includes rain, snow, hail, and sleet—essentially any moisture falling from the clouds.

q: 22. A canal aligned nearly parallel to the contours of a country, is known is
explain: A contour canal follows the natural contours, allowing it to irrigate the land on the downhill side.

q: 23. Which of the following is the correct sequence of the parts of a canal system?
options: Head works, distributary, branch canals and minor
Head works, main canal, branch canal, distributary and minor
Head works, main canal, branch canal, branch canal, minor and distributary
explain: The standard hierarchy is Main Canal → Branch Canal → Distributary → Minor → Watercourse.

q: 24. The saturation gradient in an ordinary loam soils is, usually, kept from
explain: The saturation line (phreatic line) in loam soil banks is typically assumed to have a slope of 4:1 for design stability.

q: 25. A spoil bank is formed when the
options: volume of excavation is in excess of the embankment filling
explain: When the earth excavated from the canal is more than what is needed for the banks, the surplus is piled into 'spoil banks'.

q: 26. When the quantity of the earth is much in excess of the quantity required for filling, it has to be deposited in the form of spoil banks. The spoil banks are made on
explain: Depending on available land and the volume of excess soil, spoil banks can be constructed on either or both sides of the canal alignment.

q: 27. Lining of a canal is necessary
options: to minimize the seepage losses in canal
to prevent erosion of bed and sides due to high velocities
to increase the discharge in canal section by increasing the velocity
explain: Lining creates a smooth, impermeable surface that saves water, allows for higher non-erodible velocities, and improves discharge capacity.

q: 28. Lining of canal ............. the maintenance of the canal.
explain: Lining prevents weed growth and silting, which significantly reduces the frequency and cost of annual maintenance.

q: 29. According to Lacey
options: the silt is kept in suspension due to the force of vertical eddies
the eddies are generated from bed and sides, both normal to the surface of generation
the vertical component of eddies generated from sides will also support the silt
explain: Unlike Kennedy, Lacey accounted for eddies generated from the entire wetted perimeter (bed and sides).

q: 30. Lacey gave a relation between
explain: Lacey provided a comprehensive set of equations relating $V$, $R$, $A$, $Q$, and $S$ for regime channels.

q: 31. The general regime flow equation is
explain: This is Lacey's general flow equation derived for regime channels in alluvium.

q: 32. Cross regulators are provided
options: to raise the water level to its upstream during the periods of low discharges in the parent channel
to help in closing the supply to downstream of the parent channel
to absorb fluctuation in various sections of the canal system
explain: Cross regulators are built across the main canal to back up water for off-takes and control flow downstream.

q: 33. The capacity of escape channel should not be less than ............. of the capacity of the parent channel at that point.
explain: To be effective as an emergency safety structure, an escape must be able to handle at least 50% of the canal's design discharge.

q: 34. In Sarda type fall, the length of the crest is kept ............. the bed width of the canal.
explain: Standard design for a Sarda fall keeps the crest length equal to the bed width of the incoming canal.

q: 35. A sudden fall of level of ground along the alignment of a canal joined by an inclined bed is called a
explain: Rapid falls consist of a long sloping glacis and are used where the natural ground slope is steeper than the canal bed slope.

q: 36. In a proportional outlet, the rate of change of its discharge is ............. the rate of change of the discharge of the distributing channel.
explain: Proportionality means that if the parent canal discharge increases by 10%, the outlet discharge also increases by 10%.

q: 37. An outlet is said to be proportional, if its flexibility is
explain: Flexibility is defined as the ratio of the rate of change of discharge of an outlet to the rate of change of discharge of the distributing channel. When this ratio is 1 (unity), the outlet is proportional.

q: 38. Which of the following is a type of non-modular outlet?
explain: A submerged pipe outlet is a non-modular outlet because its discharge depends on the difference in water levels between the distributary and the watercourse.

q: 39. Which of the following is a type of semi-module outlet?
explain: Semi-modules (or flexible modules) like open flume outlets and Kennedy's gauge outlets have discharges that depend only on the water level in the distributary, independent of the watercourse level.

q: 40. In Bligh's creep theory, it is assumed that the percolation water creep .............
options: along the contact of the base profile of the apron with the sub-soil
in a straight path under the floor
in a straight path under the foundation work
explain: Bligh's theory assumes water 'creeps' along the entire length of the contact surface between the structure's base and the soil.

q: 41. In Lane's weighted creep theory, he proposed a weight of .............
options: three for vertical creep and one for horizontal creep
three for horizontal creep and one for vertical creep
two for vertical and two for horizontal creep
explain: Lane suggested that vertical surfaces are three times more effective in resisting piping than horizontal surfaces, thus weightage is 3 for vertical and 1 for horizontal creep.

q: 42. In a barrage, crest level is kept .............
explain: Barrages typically have a low crest level to allow maximum flood discharge; large gates are then used to control and raise the water level when needed.

q: 43. The loss of head per unit length of creep is called .............
explain: This represents the hydraulic gradient under the structure. Bligh defined the reciprocal of this (length/head) as the Coefficient of Creep (C), but head loss per unit length is the percolation coefficient.

q: 44. According to Khosla's theory, the exit gradient in the absence of a downstream cut-off is .............
explain: Without a vertical cut-off at the end of the floor, the exit gradient becomes theoretically infinite, leading to immediate piping and failure.

q: 45. In a siphon, the underside of the trough carrying drainage water is ............. the F.S.L. of the canal.
explain: In a canal siphon (or siphon aqueduct), the structure is designed such that the canal FSL is actually higher than the bottom of the crossing trough, forcing water to flow under pressure.

q: 46. The floor of the aqueduct is subjected to uplift pressure due to .............
options: seepage of water from the canal to the drainage
sub-soil water table in the drainage bed
explain: Uplift on the floor can be caused by both the static water table in the surrounding soil and the seepage of water from the canal itself.

q: 47. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following. Culturable commanded area is the gross area of an irrigation canal system less .............
explain: Fallow land is technically culturable. CCA is GCA minus non-culturable areas like towns, roads, forests, and barren (alkaline) lands.

q: 48. In gravity canals, F.S.L. is .............
options: generally 4 to 5 meters above the ground level
only a few cm above the ground level
explain: For efficient gravity flow into fields, the canal water level (FSL) should be slightly higher than the surrounding ground level.

q: 49. If d1 is the depth of cutting, d2 is the height of the bank... the horizontal distance n between the bed and bank, is .............
explain: The horizontal distance depends on the slope ($r$) and the height ($d$) of the bank; hence $x = r_2 \times d_2$.

q: 50. The saturation line is the line up to which banks get saturated after the canal runs for some time. The saturation gradient in ordinary loam soil, is generally .............
explain: In ordinary loam, the phreatic line (seepage line) usually follows a gradient of 4 horizontal to 1 vertical.

q: 51. If the straight sides... make an angle θ with horizontal, the perimeter of the canal is .............
explain: For the same rounded triangular section, the wetted perimeter $P = 2R (\theta + \cot \theta)$.

q: 52. The ratio of the discharge over a trapezoidal crest to a rectangular crest of Sarda falls of identical parameters, is .............
explain: A trapezoidal crest has a slightly higher discharge coefficient due to its shape, resulting in a ratio of approximately 1.084 compared to a rectangular crest.

q: 53. The depth of the crest of a scouring sluice below the crest of a head regulator, is generally kept .............
explain: A difference of 1.2 meters is standard to allow for a 'silt pocket' where heavier sediment can settle and be flushed out.

q: 54. According to Khosla, the exists gradient of surface flow .............
options: is independent of the b/d ratio
is independent of the depths of d/s cut off walls
explain: Exit gradient depends on the ratio of floor length (b) to the depth of the downstream end pile (d).

q: 55. The width of a meander belt is the transverse distance between .............
options: apex point of one curve and apex point of the reserve curve
explain: Meander belt width is the total width of the valley occupied by the river as it swings from one extreme apex to the other.

q: 56. A deficit of sediments in flowing water may cause a river .............
explain: If the water has less sediment than its carrying capacity, it will scour the bed to pick up more, leading to 'degradation'.
